record.original_question: Can one determine a single model together with an adequate optimization technique that simultaneously accounts for many different characteristics of computer-network operation quality?

evidence.quote: Another open problem consists in determining a single model that enables to consider many different characteristics of the quality of network operation and an adequate technique to optimize them.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Model a computer network as a directed graph G = (V, E) where V is the set of nodes (routers/hosts) and E is the set of communication links. Each link e ∈ E is endowed with multiple time-dependent performance attributes such as bandwidth capacity c(e), latency ℓ(e), packet-loss probability p(e), jitter j(e), energy consumption ε(e), reliability/availability r(e), and monetary cost κ(e). A set K of commodities (source–destination demands) must be routed through G, and the resulting flow assignment induces aggregate quality-of-operation measures Q_1, Q_2, …, Q_m (e.g., total throughput, worst-case end-to-end delay, mean loss, fairness, robustness to failures, energy efficiency, and operating cost).

Problem. Construct a single mathematical optimization model
   minimize / maximize F(Q_1(x), Q_2(x), …, Q_m(x))
   subject to x ∈ 𝒳(G, demands),
together with a tractable algorithmic technique to solve it, such that:

(a) the model simultaneously incorporates the heterogeneous quality-of-operation criteria Q_1, …, Q_m (which may be of different physical units, may be conflicting, and may be stochastic or time-varying);
(b) the feasible set 𝒳 captures realistic networking constraints (flow conservation, link capacities, routing policies, queueing behavior);
(c) the optimization technique produces solutions (Pareto-optimal or scalarized) with provable guarantees on running time or approximation quality, and scales to networks of practical size.

Does such a unified model together with an adequate optimization technique exist?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad open research direction concerning a unified multi-criteria network-optimization framework. No single accepted unified model with an adequate general-purpose optimization technique covering all major network quality characteristics is known; the literature offers many partial, criterion-specific or bi-objective approaches. Status remains open.

status_evidence.title: Multi-objective optimization in computer networks (survey overview)
status_evidence.snippet: States that determining a single model accounting for many different characteristics of network operation quality, together with an adequate optimization technique, remains an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The unified multi-criteria network optimization problem is explicitly listed as open.
